summary: Markets took a breather Monday after hitting fresh highs last week, with the S&P 500 slipping 0.06% as oil prices surged nearly 5% on renewed Middle East tensions. WTI crude topped $80 per barrel following Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries and stalled Iran-Oman negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz, pushing 10-year Treasury yields up six basis points to 4.71% and reviving inflation concerns ahead of Wednesday's critical July CPI release. The Fed's divided 9-3 vote at its July 29 meeting—the most dissent since 2016—has left markets on edge, with three regional Fed presidents dissenting in favor of rate hikes as Chair Warsh holds the line at 3.50-3.75%. Crypto markets posted a contrasting picture: Bitcoin ETFs drew over $850 million in weekly inflows, the strongest performance since April, led by BlackRock's IBIT with $693 million. Ethereum ETFs extended their streak to four consecutive days of inflows, pulling in $50 million on August 7 alone. Nvidia shares fell 3% on reports of a $500 billion AI infrastructure funding partnership with Apollo Global and Blackstone, weighing on tech indexes.

signals.title: Oil spike revives inflation fears ahead of CPI
signals.desc: WTI crude surged 5% to above $80/barrel on Middle East tensions, pushing Treasury yields to 4.71% and raising concerns that Wednesday's July CPI print could complicate the Fed's rate path.

signals.title: Fed's most divided vote since 2016 signals hawk-dove split
signals.desc: The FOMC's 9-3 decision on July 29 to hold rates at 3.50-3.75% marked the most dissent in eight years, with three regional presidents voting for hikes, leaving September policy unclear.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs post $850M weekly inflows, best since April
signals.desc: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted over $850 million last week led by BlackRock's IBIT with $693M, signaling institutional demand recovery after brutal first-half outflows.

signals.title: Nvidia drops 3% on $500B AI infrastructure funding news
signals.desc: Nvidia shares fell nearly 3% on reports of a massive AI infrastructure funding package with Apollo and Blackstone, weighing on the Nasdaq as investors digest capex scale.

signals.title: Ethereum ETFs extend inflow streak to four days
signals.desc: Spot Ethereum ETFs pulled in $49.60 million on August 7, marking the fourth consecutive day of inflows at $244.94 million for the week, though volumes remain modest versus Bitcoin products.

verdict: Markets face a critical inflection point with Wednesday's CPI release likely to determine whether the Fed can cut in September or hawkish dissenters gain the upper hand amid oil-driven inflation fears.
